core_claim.quote: Ignition is characterized by the sudden, coherent, and exclusive activation of a subset of workspace neurons coding for the current conscious content, with the remainder of the workspace neurons being inhibited.

source.citation: Mashour GA, Roelfsema P, Changeux J-P, Dehaene S. Conscious processing and the global neuronal workspace hypothesis. Neuron 105(5):776-798, 2020

prediction.statement: Between the onset and offset ignitions, a lasting percept is held in an 'activity-silent' state, not by sustained activity.

first_stated.passage: GNW assumes that all experiences – regardless of their temporal extent – are accompanied by an initial ignition, followed by a decay of signal and maintenance of information in the form of an activity-silent state, with only occasional bursts of reactivation

source.citation: Melloni L, Mudrik L, Pitts M, et al. Preregistration file v1, January 2019: Accelerating research on consciousness: an adversarial collaboration to test contradictory predictions of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theory. OSF project mbcfy, component wz8mj

prediction.test_for: Prefrontal activity returns to baseline between onset and offset of a lasting conscious stimulus, with no sustained content-specific activity there.
prediction.test_against: Sustained content-specific prefrontal activity for the whole duration of the percept.

what_the_sources_say_about_rivals.statement: IIT predicts sustained content-specific activity (in posterior cortex) for the whole percept.
